title: perf-bench-latency-throughput-notes-ashley-2026-03-08
content:
Quick notes from local perf runs (scratchpad)

Date: 2026-03-07 / 2026-03-08 (ran multiple iterations)
Owner: Ashley Nguyen (notes v1 -> v2)
Context: trying to reproduce the odd P95 spikes seen in staging for short-chat workloads. Focused on 2 model variants: redwood-v1-small (int8) and redwood-v1-medium (fp16).

Hardware / infra used
- Dedicated test node: g4dn-like instance (NVIDIA T4), 16GB GPU memory, 8 vCPUs, 64GB RAM
- Runtime: rwd-infer 1.12.0-local build (feature branch: perf/kvcache-batching)
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
- Network: single AZ, no cross-region routing

Experiment matrix (high level)
- Models: redwood-v1-small-int8, redwood-v1-medium-fp16
- KV cache: enabled vs disabled
- Batching: none (1), small (batch_size=8), medium (batch_size=32)
- Sequence lengths: short (prompt ~40 tokens, gen 40 tokens), medium (prompt 128, gen 128)
- Concurrency: 1, 8, 32 parallel clients (wrk-style)
- Warmup: 120s, then 300s measurement windows

Commands used
- launcher: ./rwd-bench --model redwood-v1-small-int8 --concurrency 8 --batch 8 --kv-cache on --seq 40/40 --duration 300 --out results/small_b8_kv_on_8c.json
- profiler: rwd-trace top --pid <runtime_pid> --duration 60
- latency capture: /usr/local/bin/lat-capture --p95 --p50 --hist --out hist_small_kv_on.txt

Raw observations (summary)
- Baseline (no batch, kv-cache off, concurrency=1): P50 ~ 22ms, P95 ~ 44ms, tokens/s ~ 180
- Batch=8, kv-cache on, concurrency=8: P50 ~ 28ms, P95 ~ 85ms (occasional spikes to 200-400ms), tokens/s ~ 2200
- Batch=32, kv-cache on, concurrency=32: P50 ~ 60ms, P95 ~ 320ms, throughput saturates around 7.5k tokens/s, but latency tail is bad
- KV-cache disabled at higher conc: throughput drops ~15%-25% and CPU/host-side latency increases more than GPU time savings

Notes on spikes
- Spikes correlate with GC/host pauses when concurrent client count > 8. Trace shows a 100-300ms host-side stall outside of GPU kernel time.
- Spikes less frequent when using smaller batches (8) but still present. Suspect: host-side queue + batch formation logic + occasional mallocs in batching library (we use an internal pooling strategy that might not be warmed up).
- rwd-trace shows periodic memcpy stalls when kv-cache is enabled and sequence lengths vary (e.g., mixing 40/40 requests with a handful of 128/128). Might be application-level copying of past KV states into preallocated buffers.

Throughput vs latency tradeoffs (observed)
- For 40/40 small chat use-case we can get high throughput with batching 8-16 and 8-16 concurrency while maintaining acceptable P95 (~<100ms).
- For mixed-length traffic the batching algorithm sometimes coalesces to larger effective sequences, increasing kernel time per batch and causing latency tail. Need sequence-aware batching.

Quick chart-like summaries (approx)
- redwood-v1-small-int8, seq 40/40, kv on:
  - conc=1 batch=1 -> P50 22ms P95 44ms TPS 180
  - conc=8 batch=8 -> P50 28ms P95 85ms TPS 2200
  - conc=32 batch=32 -> P50 60ms P95 320ms TPS 7500

- redwood-v1-medium-fp16, seq 128/128, kv on:
  - conc=1 batch=1 -> P50 120ms P95 210ms TPS 65
  - conc=8 batch=8 -> P50 165ms P95 430ms TPS 480

Hypotheses to validate
1) Host-side memory traffic (memcpy of KV blocks) is causing stalls when requests of mixed seq lengths hit same worker. Instrument allocator and buffer reuse paths.
2) Batching logic does not sufficiently prioritize low-latency requests; implement max-delay for latency-sensitive routes.
3) GC/allocator behavior under high concurrency (node-level) causing pauses; try jemalloc or pre-touch buffers.

Immediate next steps
- Re-run with jemalloc preloaded on node (compare with system malloc) and capture latency histograms (Jordan to help) - target: reduce P95 spikes by >=30%
- Add additional tracing around KV-copy path (Samira will add brief logging around buffer copy counts and sizes)
- Experiment with sequence-aware batching threshold: disallow coalescing requests where seq_diff > 64 tokens
- Re-run mixed-length test (90/10 split short/long) and look at spike frequency

Things to copy into ticket/PR
- GH-PR-4821: patch that adds preallocated per-worker KV buffers and a fast-path when sizes match exactly. Patch is on branch perf/kvcache-batching.
- JIRA-RUNS-215: epic to track stable perf baseline for chat workload (includes infra config and bench harness)
- Confluence: perf-run notes page (CONFLUENCE-ENG-1234) - paste initial numbers and add slow-stack traces

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Is the memcpy coming from our C++ runtime or from Python shim? Confirm with symbolized traces.
- Check NVTX ranges to see if kernel queueing matches host-side queueing (are we batching too early or too late?)
- Should we add a per-request priority hint to avoid batching high-priority latency requests with large long-running ones?

Scratch commands to re-run quickly
- jemalloc: LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libjemalloc.so ./rwd-bench --model redwood-v1-small-int8 --concurrency 32 --batch 8 --kv-cache on --seq 40/40 --duration 300
- mixed: ./rwd-bench --mixed-ratio 90:10 --short 40/40 --long 128/128 --concurrency 16 --batch 16 --kv-cache on --duration 300

Notes appended 2026-03-08: Ran jemalloc test (one warmup run) - initial glance: P95 spikes reduced ~18% but still present. Need more runs to be confident.

End of scratchpad. Will tidy and create a proper run log + upload JSON traces to JIRA epic after next stable run.
